task: E13 browser proof harness compatibility and quality authority reconciliation for the canonical workforce entry contract.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The change is limited to quality/proof infrastructure but its output is release evidence. A defective harness can create false negatives that block valid releases or, worse, false positives that certify an invalid exact-head state. Product runtime identity and authorization authority must remain unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria: The E13 browser proof authenticates through /api/auth/workforce-login with next=/admin/platform instead of navigating to the removed legacy /platform password form.
The proof waits for the canonical data-workforce-auth surface and uses its email/password inputs and canonical submit control.
The proof reaches /admin/platform after the canonical workforce entry without changing product runtime authentication, role, tenant or MFA authority.
The canonical domain registry classifies the Template Factory Product Owner handoff and Template Factory quality-gate scripts as DOMAIN-QUALITY / quality-knowledge-system infrastructure.
Regression tests fail if the proof producer returns to the legacy /platform credential surface or if the quality script loses canonical DOMAIN-QUALITY classification.
PR #858 remains parked; no AAL2 enforcement or product runtime behavior is activated or weakened.
invariants: A failing acceptance harness must be repaired at the harness/quality authority when the product contract is already correct.
The proof harness may consume the canonical workforce entry contract but may not become authentication or authorization authority.
Production/runtime auth, tenant, role and middleware files remain read-only.
The Release Risk Budget must see only the quality-infrastructure release subsystem plus neutral tests/plan metadata.
The proof must still require real credentials, canonical navigation to /admin/platform and the existing E13 side-effect/fail-closed assertions.

failureModes: The E13 harness still opens /platform and waits for the deleted legacy Belépés a Shoperationbe button.
The harness navigates to canonical workforce login but queries generic inputs outside the workforce surface and can bind to the wrong form.
The harness stops checking that the resulting route is /admin/platform, turning identity entry into a shallow page-load proof.
The product runtime is modified to satisfy the old harness instead of repairing the stale evidence producer.
The handoff script remains outside DOMAIN-QUALITY even though release and knowledge policies already classify it as quality infrastructure.
A broad domain path reclassifies unrelated Template Factory implementation as quality authority.
The proof compatibility fix is mixed back into the ADMIN/BUILDER/STOREFRONT delegator release and recreates the Release Risk Budget violation.
edgeCases: An existing storageState may already reach /admin/platform and remains a valid fast path.
Without stored state, missing proof credentials still fails closed with ENGINE_FUNCTIONAL_PLATFORM_CREDENTIALS_REQUIRED.
Canonical workforce login may present its own session/MFA continuation; the harness must not reimplement that authority.
The classification change uses exact script paths rather than a broad scripts/template-factory-** ownership claim.
The E13 proof retains cookie-consent handling, role-required diagnostics, authoritative quote, checkout flow and no-production-side-effect assertions.

alternatives.summary: Change /platform back to the old direct password form so the proof can log in.
alternatives.reason: That would regress the verified Workforce Auth convergence and make product runtime conform to stale test infrastructure.

alternatives.summary: Bypass or mark the exact-head E13 browser proof optional for this release.
alternatives.reason: External functional proof is part of the canonical completion contract; removing it would weaken assurance.

alternatives.summary: Update only the quality proof producer to consume the canonical workforce entry and reconcile its DOMAIN-QUALITY ownership.
alternatives.reason: This repairs the stale evidence path without changing product authority and keeps the release-risk transaction isolated.

specialistReviews.finding: The handoff and quality-gate scripts are already treated as quality infrastructure by scope/release policy but lack canonical DOMAIN-QUALITY path ownership.
specialistReviews.resolution: Register only the two exact quality scripts under DOMAIN-QUALITY; do not claim all Template Factory scripts.

specialistReviews.finding: Changing the product to satisfy the old E13 selector would convert a harness defect into a product regression.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep product runtime read-only and update authenticatePlatformOperator to traverse the canonical workforce entry while retaining all downstream E13 proof obligations.

specialistReviews.finding: The proof-harness edit cannot remain mixed with the delegator release because Release Risk Budget becomes 7/5 across four subsystems.
specialistReviews.resolution: Ship the quality-infrastructure compatibility change first as its own release, then rebase/reconstruct the delegator release on the new main.

challenge.scenario: The proof opens /platform after the product removed direct password entry.
challenge.finding: The proof fails before testing E13 even though the canonical product entry is correct.

challenge.scenario: Another form with email/password inputs is present on the page.
challenge.finding: Generic selectors could authenticate through the wrong surface.

challenge.scenario: Canonical sign-in succeeds but the actor lacks platform authority.
challenge.finding: A shallow login success could falsely satisfy the engine precondition.
challenge.resolution: Retain the /admin/platform URL wait and ENGINE_FUNCTIONAL_PLATFORM_ROLE_REQUIRED diagnostic.

challenge.scenario: A developer repairs the failure by reintroducing the old product login UI.
challenge.finding: The acceptance harness would pass while the verified identity architecture regresses.
challenge.resolution: Product runtime auth files are impacted-read-only and regression tests assert the harness contract instead.

challenge.scenario: The quality script remains unowned in Atlas.
challenge.finding: Future Plan Before Code/Authority Graph reasoning can treat a canonical proof producer as semantically unresolved.
challenge.resolution: Add only the exact handoff and quality-gate script paths to DOMAIN-QUALITY and prove classification.

challenge.scenario: The domain fix broadly labels all Template Factory scripts as quality.
challenge.finding: Builder implementation authority could be stolen by a broad quality glob.
challenge.resolution: Use two exact canonical paths matching the scripts already named by knowledge/release policy.

challenge.scenario: The proof-harness fix stays in PR #912.
challenge.finding: Release Risk Budget remains 7/5, 4/3 and blocks before functional proof.
challenge.resolution: Isolate this quality release first; PR #912 will later consume it from main with no quality-infrastructure diff.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code on the exact plan-only quality-infrastructure head before editing the domain registry or proof producer.
Add exact DOMAIN-QUALITY ownership for the two existing Template Factory quality scripts.
Change only authenticatePlatformOperator in the E13 proof producer to use canonical workforce entry; retain downstream proof semantics.
Add deterministic source-contract regression for the canonical workforce selectors and semantic Atlas regression for DOMAIN-QUALITY ownership.
Run Edit-Time Guard and full Incremental Known Failure Replay because quality knowledge changes force full replay.
Require Release Risk Budget PASS with quality-infrastructure only.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build, then exact-head Completion Truth and lifecycle closure before merge.

requirements.requirement: The E13 exact-head browser proof consumes the canonical workforce entry contract and the proof producer is owned by canonical quality authority without changing product runtime identity or authorization semantics.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The E13 proof must not depend on the removed legacy /platform direct-password surface.
Product runtime identity/authorization behavior must not be weakened or changed to satisfy the proof producer.
The canonical Template Factory proof scripts must not remain semantically unclassified.

requirements.requirement: The proof-harness compatibility ships as an isolated quality-infrastructure release within the canonical Release Risk Budget.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The quality proof-harness change must not ship in the same release diff as substantive ADMIN/BUILDER/STOREFRONT delegator changes.

notes: PR #912 proved the product delegator release itself is valid but a later exact-head E13 proof exposed a stale quality harness coupled to the removed legacy /platform password UI. Keeping the harness edit in #912 raises Release Risk Budget from the delegator-only 5/5 across 3 subsystems to 7/5 across 4. This transaction isolates the quality-infrastructure fix first. Product runtime and parked PR #858 remain untouched.
